sheet.title: Mythic Bastionland
sheet.empty: Nothing yet. Drag an item here or add one.
sheet.newKnightHint: Roll up a Knight from the book on this sheet. The new scores, Property, Ability and Passion replace the ones here. Scars stay.

heraldry.title: Heraldry of {name}
heraldry.lineHint: Drag from one end to the other. Hold Shift to keep it level, upright or diagonal.
heraldry.eyedropperHint: Click the shield to take a colour from it. Alt-click does the same with any tool.
heraldry.divisionsHint: Pick a division, then click a part of the shield to paint it, and the parts matching it, in the colour in hand.
heraldry.downloadHint: Save this design to your computer, to upload again later.
heraldry.downloadFailed: The design could not be turned into a file to download.

placing.title: Placing a picture
placing.hint: Drag it to move it. Scroll over it, or use the slider, to change its size. Place it to paint it in.

charges.openHint: Place a lion, a tower, a star or another charge on the shield, in the colour in hand.
charges.title: Charges
charges.hint: Click a charge to place it on the shield in the colour in hand.
charges.credit: Drawn after public-domain heraldry books by Mathghamhain Ua Ruadháin for the Book of Traceable Heraldic Art. © 2016–2023 Matthew Simon Ryan Cavalletto, CC BY-SA 4.0.

heraldry.randomizeHint: Paint random arms over the whole shield: a field, plain or divided, and perhaps a charge, in tinctures that read well against each other. Undo brings the last design back.
heraldry.unreadable: That picture couldn’t be loaded onto the shield.
heraldry.tooLarge: This heraldry is too detailed to keep on the Knight. Simplify it, or ask the GM to let you upload files.

vig.label: Vigour
vig.hint: Strong limbs, firm hands, powerful lungs.

cla.label: Clarity
cla.hint: Keen instinct, lucid mind, shrewd eyes.

spi.label: Spirit
spi.hint: Charming tongue, iron will, fierce heart.

glory.label: Glory
glory.title: Glory
glory.hint: Won when a Myth you played a part in is resolved, by a staked duel or joust, a tournament, a battle remembered in history, or when a new Age begins.
glory.nobody: Nobody was ticked, so no Glory is awarded.

myth.label: Myth Resolved
myth.intro: Tick every Knight who played a part in the Myth. Each gains 1 Glory.
myth.hint: When the group feels that a Myth has reached a conclusion of any type.

tournament.label: Tournament Won
tournament.intro: Tick the winning Knight. They gain 1 Glory.
tournament.hint: Only a tournament with significant spectators and spectacle grants Glory.

battle.label: Battle Won
battle.intro: Tick every Knight on the victorious side. Each gains 1 Glory.
battle.hint: Only a battle large enough to be remembered in history grants Glory.

successor.label: Successor
successor.hint: The Knight or Squire named to follow this Knight. Succession names them, and Legacy passes on half of this Knight’s Glory.
successor.empty: No successor named. Drop a Knight here, or choose one.
successor.name: Name a Successor
successor.title: Name a Successor
successor.intro: Whom does {name} name as their successor?
successor.none: There’s no other Knight or Squire in this world for {name} to name.
successor.noLegacy: Legacy: no successor named, so no Glory passes on.
successor.legacy: Legacy: {name} gains {amount} Glory, half of theirs.

seer.label: Seer
seer.unnamed: Write the Seer who knighted them on the Knight page, beside “Knighted by”. A Seer from the book fills in their picture and what the book says.
seer.squire: A Squire isn’t a Knight yet (p7). Once a Seer knights them, write the Seer’s name beside “Knighted by” on the Knight page.
seer.infoEmpty: Filled in from the book once the Seer beside “Knighted by” is one of the book’s and Import PDF has been run.

squire.label: Squire
squire.rules: An apprentice with 2d6 in each Virtue and 1GD, riding a pony (VIG 7, CLA 7, SPI 2, 2GD) and carrying a dagger (d6) and a d6 roll of extra equipment. Not yet a Knight, so they can’t gain Glory or perform Feats. When Knighted they gain d6 in each Virtue.
squire.empty: Small Companies of 2 Knights or fewer may give each Knight a Squire. Take one, or drag a Squire here from the Actors tab.
squire.servesNobody: A Squire who serves no Knight. Drag this Squire onto a Knight’s sheet.
squire.hint: An apprentice, not yet a Knight, so they can’t gain Glory or perform Feats. When Knighted they gain d6 in each Virtue.
squire.noFeats: Squires can’t perform Feats until they are Knighted.
squire.name: Squire to {knight}
squire.title: A Squire
squire.largeCompany: Only Companies of 2 Knights or fewer may give each Knight a Squire, and this one has {count}. Take a Squire anyway?
squire.largeCompanyPlayer: Only Companies of 2 Knights or fewer may give each Knight a Squire, and this one has {count}. Ask the Referee.
squire.largeCompanyHint: The Company has {count} Knights, and only Companies of 2 or fewer may give each Knight a Squire.
squire.largeCompanyHintGM: The Company has {count} Knights, and only Companies of 2 or fewer may give each Knight a Squire. As Referee you may grant one anyway.
squire.companyGrew: The Company now has {count} Knights, and only Companies of 2 or fewer may give each Knight a Squire. Squires in this world: {squires}. Whether they stay is the Referee’s call.
squire.cantCreate: Taking a Squire creates them and their pony, so it needs a user who is allowed to create actors.
squire.knightConfirm: {name} becomes a Knight, gaining d6 in each Virtue. From then on they can gain Glory and perform Feats.

rank.label: Rank
rank.hint: Rank alone doesn’t grant a Council position or rule of a Holding. It merely proves worthiness. A Knight in a position their rank is unworthy of is sure to face opposition, but if they overcome it their worthiness is proven.

worthy.gallant: Worthy of a seat in Council or Court
worthy.dominant: Worthy of ruling a Seat of Power

fatigued.label: Fatigued
fatigued.hint: Cannot perform Feats until they rest.

exhausted.label: Exhausted
exhausted.hint: At VIG 0 you cannot Attack if you have moved this turn.

exposed.label: Exposed
exposed.hint: Treated as having 0GD. CLA 0 also leaves you Exposed.

impaired.label: Impaired
impaired.hint: At SPI 0 your Attacks roll a single d4 only.

mortalWound.label: Mortal Wound
mortalWound.hint: Down and dying. They die if left untended for an hour, but can be patched up in a few moments.

recovery.label: Recovery
recovery.rested: A moment’s calm: GD restored to {value} and Fatigue removed.

oath.label: Oath
oath.hint: Every Knight has sworn the Oath.

knighthood.title: Knighthood
knighthood.intro1: You are Knights, united by a common Oath and visions of the City. You may have dreams of glory, but every Knight must accept the risk of death.
knighthood.intro2: The Seers who knighted you have deemed that you travel as a Company. While some of you may rest, roam, or die, your collective journey will be as one.
knighthood.virtues: Knights have 3 Virtues. Roll a value for each in order. The Start chosen for your Company sets the dice; if unsure, roll d12+d6.
knighthood.guard: Roll for Guard (GD), your skill at avoiding Wounds. The Start chosen for your Company sets the dice; if unsure, roll d6.
knighthood.chooseKnight: Roll or choose a Knight (p26). This gives:
knighthood.kit: Has a dagger (d6), torches, rope, dry rations, and camping gear.
knighthood.oath: Has sworn the Oath: Seek the Myths, Honour the Seers, Protect the Realm.
knighthood.squires1: Small Companies (2 Knights or fewer) may give each Knight a Squire. They serve as apprentices, and are not yet Knights, so cannot gain Glory or perform Feats.
knighthood.squires2: 2d6 for each Virtue, 1GD. They ride a pony (VIG 7, CLA 7, SPI 2, 2GD) and carry a dagger (d6).
knighthood.squires3: Roll d6 for their extra equipment: 1 Cudgel (d8 hefty), 2 Axe (d8 hefty), 3 Hatchet (d6), 4 Shortbow (d6 long), 5 Shield (d4, A1), 6 Three Javelins (d6).
knighthood.squires4: When Knighted they gain d6 in each Virtue.
knighthood.glory: All Knights seek Glory, that they might one day be deemed worthy of the City Quest.
knighthood.gloryMythsText: When the group feels that a Myth has been resolved, reaching a conclusion of any type, all Knights who played a part in it gain 1 Glory.
knighthood.gloryDuel: In a public duel or joust, Knights may stake Glory against a willing opponent. The victor gains 1 Glory, the loser loses 1.
knighthood.gloryTournament: A tournament may grant 1 Glory to the winning Knight, provided there are significant spectators and spectacle.
knighthood.gloryBattle: If a battle is large enough to be remembered in history, all Knights on the victorious side gain 1 Glory.
knighthood.gloryAge: When the game moves to a new Age, all Knights gain 1 Glory through serving the Realm and manoeuvring in Court.

property.label: Property
property.hint: Items brought with you. Every Knight also has a dagger (d6), torches, rope, dry rations, and camping gear.

steed.label: Steed
steed.empty: Drag an NPC from the Actors tab here to ride it. Its trample joins a mounted charge.
steed.fromDirectory: Drag the steed from the Actors tab rather than a compendium, so it can be targeted in combat.

remedy.intro: Tick everybody present. Each has their {virtue} restored, and the Remedy is used up.
remedy.hint: Using a Remedy takes a whole Phase. The Virtue is restored before any Omens or other encounters.

ability.label: Ability
ability.hint: A special talent unique to you.

passion.label: Passion
passion.hint: A special means you have to restore your Spirit.

feats.label: Feats
feats.knightHint: Every Knight knows the three Feats.

smite.name: Smite
smite.summary: +d12 or Blast to a melee attack.
smite.use: Use before rolling a melee Attack. The Attack gains either +d12 or Blast.

focus.name: Focus
focus.summary: Perform a Gambit without using a die.
focus.use: Use after rolling an Attack. Perform a Gambit without using a die.

deny.name: Deny
deny.tagline: Rebuff an attack before it lands
deny.summary: Discard a damage die rolled against you or a nearby Ally.
deny.use: Use after an Attack roll against you or an ally within arm’s reach. Discard one Attack die from the roll.

feats.alreadyFatigued: {name} is Fatigued and cannot perform Feats until they rest.

gambits.label: Gambits
gambits.stop: Stop a foe from moving next turn
gambits.impair: Impair a weapon on their next turn
gambits.trap: Trap a shield until your next turn
gambits.other: Other effect of a similar level of impact
gambits.hint: Discard Attack dice of 4 or higher, one per Gambit. Foes get a VIG Save against all but Bolster and Move.
gambits.strong: Strong Gambit: a melee die of 8+ also grants No Save or a Greater effect.

card.tagline: Gambit: discard an Attack die of 4 or higher
card.noSave: The target gets no Save against it.
card.target: The affected foe must be a target of the original Attack.

details.move: You may Move even if you already moved or are unable to move.
details.dismount: Being dismounted causes d6 Damage. In combat, add it to the Attack’s dice.

morale.title: Morale
morale.hint: Roll when Wounded, or when a group loses half its number. An organised group rolls once, on its leader’s SPI.
morale.notOwner: Only a GM or {name}’s owner can roll their Morale.

triggers.wounded: {name} is Wounded, and must pass a SPI Save to avoid rout or surrender.
triggers.halved: {name} has lost half its number, and must pass a SPI Save to avoid rout or surrender.

group.title: Wavering Morale
group.intro: {down} of {count} on this side are down. The rest must pass a SPI Save to avoid rout or surrender.
group.noneStanding: Nobody you control in this group is still standing.

organised.label: Organised
organised.hint: An organised group rolls once, on its leader’s SPI.

disorganised.label: Disorganised
disorganised.hint: A disorganised group rolls for each individual, on their own SPI.

duel.title: Duel
duel.buttonHint: Target the one Token you’ve agreed to duel, then press this.
duel.needTarget: Target the one Token you’ve agreed to duel, then press Duel.
duel.intro: {name} and {opponent} agree to fight. They fight as normal, but their Attacks are rolled and resolved at the same time, including the effects of Gambits, and both can use Feats before they’re resolved.

duel.label: Duel
duel.hint: Two combatants who mutually agree to fight.

duel.stakeHint: In a public duel or joust, Knights may stake Glory against a willing opponent. The victor gains 1 Glory, and the loser loses 1.
duel.stakeKnightsOnly: Only two Knights can stake Glory, and a Squire isn’t a Knight yet.
duel.bloodlessHint: Training, or a duel that isn’t to the death. Scars only come from real, deadly combat, so it leaves none.
duel.stakeNote: Glory is staked: the victor gains 1, and the loser loses 1.
duel.bloodlessNote: Bloodless: a blow that would cause a Scar leaves none.
duel.howTo: Each duelist presses Attack on their sheet, then uses Feats and declares Gambits on their card. A GM, or whoever owns both, then resolves the two Attacks together.
duel.endedNoVictor: The duel ends without a victor.
duel.attackHint: Targets the other duelist, and holds the Damage back until both Attacks are in.
duel.heldForDuel: Part of a duel: the Damage is applied from the duel card, together with the other Attack.
duel.notReady: Both duelists need to roll their Attack first.
duel.gone: One of the duelists no longer exists.
duel.attackGone: One of the duel’s Attack cards has been deleted.
duel.cantResolve: Only a GM, or somebody who owns both duelists, can resolve their Attacks.
duel.cantEnd: Only a GM, or somebody who owns both duelists, can end the duel.
duel.noScar: {name} would take a Scar, but a bloodless duel leaves none.
duel.needsGM: A GM needs to be logged in to change somebody else’s duel card.
duel.changeRefused: The duel card changed before that could be recorded.

surprise.title: Roll Surprise
surprise.intro: Tick everybody who wasn’t readied for combat. Each makes a CLA Save or misses the first turn.
surprise.hint: Players normally take the first turn, discussing their plan and acting in any order they wish.
surprise.noCombatants: This encounter has nobody in it yet.
surprise.nobody: Nobody was caught unready, so there’s nothing to roll.

time.title: Time
time.setByHand: Click a Season or Phase, or change the Age or Day, to set the calendar by hand. Only the buttons below carry out what happens between Seasons and Ages.

phaseHints.morning: Sunrise to noon. Anybody who didn’t get proper sleep loses d6 CLA, and anybody deprived of essential needs loses d6 VIG.
phaseHints.night: Sunset to sunrise. Travelling or exploring at night costs d6 SPI each, and without a guide and light the Company travels blind.

time.seasonIntro: {season} gives way to {next}. Each Knight ticked has their Virtues restored and chooses a pursuit, and any Mutilation Scar settles.
time.ageIntro: Age {age} begins in Spring. Each Knight ticked has their Virtues restored, gains 1 Glory and chooses a pursuit. Old Knights lose d12 VIG, and any Mutilation Scar settles.
time.noCompany: There are no Knights in this world yet, and no Tokens are selected.

pilgrimage.label: Pilgrimage
pilgrimage.hint: Learn about an unknown part of the Realm.

courtesy.label: Courtesy
courtesy.hint: Establish a new contact or earn a favour.

service.label: Service
service.hint: Make a small improvement to the Realm.

duty.label: Duty
duty.hint: Make a significant improvement to the Realm.

succession.label: Succession
succession.hint: Establish a successor, or have them Knighted.

legacy.label: Legacy
legacy.hint: Your successor gains half of your current Glory.

distant.hint: Travelling to a distant Realm normally sees you arrive in the next Season.
distant.title: Journey to a Distant Realm
distant.where: Which Realm does the Company journey to? Choosing one of this world’s Realm Scenes makes it the active Scene once they arrive.
distant.intro: The Company journeys to {realm}, arriving in {season}. Each Knight ticked has their Virtues restored as the Season turns, and any Mutilation Scar settles. Nobody chooses a pursuit, since they are on the road.

time.oldAge: Old age: loses {amount} VIG, max VIG {from} → {to}.
time.doomLifts: The Season of their Doom has passed, and a Mortal Wound no longer Slays them.

due.title: Due this Season
due.crisis: The Crisis Roll for {domains} (p20), from the GM Toolkit’s Time page or each Domain’s sheet.

time.unresolvedHint: Roll an Unresolved Situation for anything important left hanging.
time.winterReminder: It’s Winter: anybody camping or travelling at night loses d6 VIG, and dire weather may keep the Company where it is.

hardship.title: Hardship
hardship.none: Nobody was ticked, so nobody loses anything.
hardship.notDamage: Virtue Loss isn’t Damage, so it can’t Mortally Wound or Slay.

night.label: Night travel
night.hint: Travelling or exploring at night costs d6 SPI each.

sleep.label: No proper sleep
sleep.hint: Each morning, all who didn’t get proper sleep the day before lose d6 CLA.

winter.label: Winter cold
winter.hint: Camping, or travelling at night, in Winter costs d6 VIG each.

supplies.label: Deprived
supplies.hint: Each morning without essential needs met, the Company each lose d6 VIG.

aging.title: Growing Older
aging.intro: {name} becomes {age}. Roll each Virtue on d12+d6 for it?

domain.seatHint: The Holding of the ruler of the whole Realm, facing the same problems on a larger scale.
domain.successorHint: Whom the ruler names to follow them. Pass On hands the Domain to them.

newRuler.name: Or by name
newRuler.hint: Choose one of the world’s Knights, or write in anybody else. A Knight chosen here rules the Domain from their sheet.

passOn.buttonHint: Succession: hand the Domain to the ruler’s successor.
passOn.title: Succession
passOn.hint: Some Realms leave the choice to a conclave of Seers or to Knights-Elector rather than the ruler.
passOn.resistance: Whoever the successor, they are sure to face at least some resistance, and should quickly establish their own authority.

conquest.buttonHint: Conquest: somebody seats themselves in this Holding and rules it.
conquest.title: Conquest
conquest.introSeat: Who seizes {name}, and with it the Realm, by force?
conquest.hint: Having the audacity to seat yourself in a Holding is often enough to make you its ruler.
conquest.turmoil: Seized by force and left unchallenged, it has a period of turmoil before adapting to the new status quo. The turmoil lasts until the Season turns.
conquest.inTurmoil: In turmoil: seized by force this Season, it hasn’t yet adapted to its new ruler.
conquest.settled: The turmoil of its conquest passes, and it adapts to the rule of {ruler}.

council.label: Council
council.hint: Council members can be given tasks lasting a Phase, a Week or a Season. They’re handled as normal actions, and failure usually brings a Crisis. Seats can be granted and revoked, but the scorned rarely go quietly.

steward.label: Steward
steward.hint: Rules in your absence, carrying your authority and the key to the treasury.

marshal.label: Marshal
marshal.hint: Trains and equips soldiers, and musters them in times of war.

sheriff.label: Sheriff
sheriff.hint: Watches for threats within the Realm, and within your own walls.

envoy.label: Envoy
envoy.hint: Manages neighbours, and gives hospitality to visitors.

circle.label: The Circle
circle.hint: Worthy visiting Knights invited to sit alongside the Council as equals.

chaos.name: Chaos
chaos.resolution: Resolved by enforcing a sense of justice.

debt.name: Debt
debt.flavour: dire need of coffer and coin

famine.name: Famine
famine.resolution: Resolved by getting food into the stores.

misery.name: Misery
misery.resolution: Resolved by raising the spirits of the people.

panic.name: Panic
panic.resolution: Resolved by making the Vassals feel safe.

doubt.name: Doubt
doubt.resolution: Resolved by asserting your authority to rule.

domain.crisisRollHint: Roll at the start of each Season, or on returning from a long absence.
domain.rolledThisSeason: The Crisis Roll has been made this Season ({season}).
domain.notRolledThisSeason: The Crisis Roll hasn’t been made this Season yet ({season}).

crisis.dilemma: Dilemma: a choice between two Crises.

collections.crisis: The coffers are filled, but a Crisis comes with it.

domain.dilemmaIntro: {name} must take on one of these Crises.
domain.dilemmaOpen: No choice was made between {options}. Add the one chosen from the sheet.
domain.misruleHint: Vassals revolt, Knights leave, and pretenders move in on their claims.
domain.misruleDue: {count} unresolved Crises: if the Season ends like this, the Domain falls into misrule.
domain.fellIntoMisrule: The Season ended with {count} unresolved Crises, and the Domain falls into misrule.
domain.collectionsHint: A Steward squeezes more from the Vassals for a war or a great project.
domain.dramaHint: Every Season brings some drama. Roll to see how the ruler is involved.
domain.muster: Can muster {count} Warbands. The Marshal decides their training and armament.
domain.designs: Grand designs: work on existing buildings is done by next Season, a new building takes a Season, and grand projects such as castles and roads take an Age.
domain.succession: Succession: a ruler usually names their successor, though some Realms leave it to a conclave of Seers or Knights-Elector. Whoever it is faces some resistance.
domain.openHint: Open the Domain this Knight rules
domain.foundHint: This Knight rules no Domain yet. Found one, or drag a Domain here from the Actors tab.
domain.ask: {name} rules no Domain yet. Found one for them? It starts with them as its ruler, beside them in the Actors tab.
domain.askNamed: {name} rules no Domain yet, but {domain} names them as its ruler. Make it theirs, or found a new Domain?
domain.cantCreate: Founding a Domain creates it, so it needs a user who is allowed to create actors. Ask the Referee, or drag an existing Domain onto this sheet.
domain.fromDirectory: Drag the Domain from the Actors tab rather than a compendium.

goods.foldersSeeded: Arms & Goods: added {items} items to the Items directory and {actors} beasts, hirelings, Warbands and structures to the Actors directory.

company.title: The Company
company.name: The Company
company.place: Place the Company on the map
company.pictureHint: One Token stands for the whole Company. It belongs to no Actor, so every player can move it.
company.notPlaced: The Company can only stand on a Realm Scene.

wanderer.name: Wanderer
wanderer.hint: Young Knights-Errant who arrive in the Realm seeking Glory. You choose where they arrive.

courtier.name: Courtier
courtier.hint: Mature Knights-Gallant with a place in Court. The Company begins at the Seat of Power.

ruler.name: Ruler
ruler.hint: Mature Knights-Tenant, one of whom rules a Holding while the Seat of Power is under a wicked influence. You choose which Holding.

company.begins: The Company begins at the Seat of Power, {hex}.

choose.wanderer: Wanderers arrive in the Realm (p6). Open the hex where they arrive and press Company here.
choose.courtier: This Realm has no Seat of Power. Open the hex where the Court sits and press Company here.
choose.ruler: One Knight rules a Holding (p6). Open the hex of that Holding and press Company here.

hexLore.title: The Lay of the Land
hexLore.hint: Each Hex is large and diverse. Roll the Spark Tables for what fills this one and write down what you made of it, so it’s the same Hex when the Company comes back (p19).
hexLore.notePlaceholder: The cliffs, the streams, the clearings and the caves.
hexLore.setMissing: Import PDF hasn’t read enough of page 22 to roll a wilderness hex.
hexLore.nothingToTell: Write what’s in the hex before telling the players about it.
hexLore.prompt: {hex} on {scene} has nothing written down yet.

prompt.name: Ask about a new hex
prompt.hint: What to do when a player’s Token comes to rest in a Realm hex nothing has been written down for. Saved per browser.

modes.open: Open the Lay of the Land

spark.title: Spark Tables
spark.hint: Roll a table for a d12 in each column, and combine the two into a prompt to improvise from.
spark.noIndex: Run the Import PDF macro with your rulebook to bring in the Spark Tables.
spark.noText: Run Import PDF again with your rulebook to bring in the Spark Tables.
spark.pageMissing: The Spark Tables on this page couldn’t be read. Import PDF’s report says why.

myths.noRealm: There’s no Realm Scene yet. Use New Realm in the Scenes tab to roll one.

gmToolkit.name: GM Toolkit
gmToolkit.noCompany: The Company isn’t on this Realm’s map
gmToolkit.relaunch: Launch the world again to get the GM Toolkit. The world was already open when the system added it.
gmToolkit.gmOnly: Only a GM can make the GM Toolkit.
gmToolkit.onlyOne: This world already has a GM Toolkit.
gmToolkit.keep: The GM Toolkit holds your notes, so the world’s last one can’t be deleted.

myths.hint: The Realm’s Myths, each with the Omen playing out and the one to come. Omens are met in order (p18). The Hex panel and the Wilderness Roll count the same Omens. For your eyes only.
myths.noText: Run Import PDF to quote each Myth’s Omens here.
myths.noneYet: The Company hasn’t met any of this Myth’s Omens yet.
myths.notePlaceholder: Who has been met, what the Company knows, where it’s heading.
myths.resolvedHint: When the group feels a Myth is resolved, a new Myth replaces it in the next Season (p27).
myths.newMythTooltip: Roll d6 and d12 on the Myths table (p27) for the Myth that replaces this one, in the same hex and under the same number.
myths.newMythRolled: A new Myth in {hex}, replacing one resolved
myths.newMythHint: Its Omens start again from the first. Undo on the Realm takes the roll back, with your notes on the old Myth.

journey.hint: Every hex the Company has come into on this Realm, the last reached first, with what you wrote about it and the Spark Tables rolled there (p19). A hex counts once the Company’s Token walks into it, or when you count a visit by hand. For your eyes only.
journey.none: The Company hasn’t come into any hex of this Realm yet. Move its Token, or count a visit from the Places page.

visits.forgetConfirm: The Company’s visits to {hex} are forgotten. What you wrote about the hex, and the Spark Tables rolled there, stay.

places.hint: Every place in the Realm and what you wrote about it: its Holdings, its Landmarks, found or not, and any other hex you’ve written about or rolled for. These are the same notes as in the Lay of the Land.
places.othersHint: Hexes with something written or rolled that hold no Holding or Landmark, such as a Myth’s hex.
places.sitesHint: Places explored in more detail than a Hex (p15).
places.noOthers: Nothing is written about any other hex yet.

time.hint: The world’s calendar (p17). The buttons carry out what the book says happens as a Phase, a Season or an Age passes.
time.crisisRollsHint: Each Domain makes the Crisis Roll at the start of a Season (p20). These haven’t made it this Season yet.

seasons.hint: A record of each Season: what you wrote about it, and what passed as it ended, as its card told the table. Turning the Season, the Age, or journeying to a distant Realm fills it in. Setting the calendar by hand doesn’t. For your eyes only.
seasons.notesPlaceholder: What the Company did, who they met, what was left hanging.

notes.hint: Your own notes. At the end of each session, ask the players about their plans and ambitions for the next one, and write them here (p16).

cityQuest.title: The City Quest
cityQuest.hint: A Company worthy of the City Quest meets an Omen of the City instead of a random Myth’s Omen when the Wilderness Roll is a 1. Roll d12 plus the Omens of the City already encountered, taking the next one down the list for a duplicate.
cityQuest.noText: Run Import PDF again to quote the Omens of the City here.
cityQuest.seen: Omens of the City encountered: {count}. The City Quest ends after Omen {end} or higher.
cityQuest.roll: Roll an Omen of the City
cityQuest.ends: Omen 18 or higher: after this Omen, the City Quest ends.

methods.text: Travelling consumes a whole Phase of the day and uses one of 3 methods:

gallop.label: Gallop
gallop.text: 2 Hexes on a non-Exhausted steed. The steed loses d6 VIG.

cruise.label: Cruise
cruise.text: 3 Hexes by boat, or by steed on a rarely-found proper road.

wildernessRoll.heading: Wilderness Roll
wildernessRoll.text: When ending a Phase in Wilderness, roll:

rows.randomOmen: Encounter the next Omen from a random Myth in this Realm.
rows.nearestOmen: Encounter the next Omen from the nearest Myth.
rows.landmark: Encounter the Hex’s Landmark. Otherwise all clear.

mythHexes.heading: Myth Hexes
mythHexes.text: Ending a Phase in the Hex containing a Myth always reveals its next Omen without making a Wilderness Roll. When possible, the Knights also get the drop on the Omen.

omens.heading: Omens
omens.text: Each Myth has 6 Omens, listed in the order in which they are encountered. The first encounter with a specific Myth is always Omen 1, the second Omen 2 etc.
omens.note: Remember primacy of action (p16). If the players want to hunt for the Wyvern’s nest they don’t have to wait for that Omen to appear if they take action themselves.

barriers.heading: Barriers
barriers.text: Travel through a Barrier is not normally possible, though locals might know a way. Attempting to travel through a Barrier wastes that Phase of the day, but still causes a Wilderness Roll.

hospitality.heading: Hospitality
hospitality.text: When sleeping indoors, do not make a Wilderness Roll. Manners dictate that hospitality be granted to travelling Knights. Longer stays warrant a favour in return.

camping.heading: Camping
camping.text: When sleeping outdoors make a Wilderness Roll as normal, ignoring Landmarks. Hostile Omens prevent proper sleep, while others may not occur at all if they are improbable as nighttime activity.

supplies.heading: Supplies
supplies.text: Knights gather food, water, and firewood as they travel, so these are not tracked. In situations where essential needs are deprived the Company each lose d6 VIG each morning.

night.heading: Night
night.text: Travelling or exploring at night causes the Company to lose d6 SPI each. If they lack a guide and light they are also travelling blind.

sleep.heading: Sleep
sleep.text: Each morning, all who did not get proper sleep the previous day lose d6 CLA.

winter.heading: Winter
winter.text: Anybody camping or travelling at night in Winter loses d6 VIG. Most Realms also risk dire weather during Winter.

blind.heading: Travelling Blind
blind.text: Travellers who find themselves roaming without a proper sense of direction, or shrouded by darkness or mist, must roll when they try to move to a new Hex.

rows.circleBack: Circle back to where you started.
rows.drift: Drift a Hex to the Left (2) or Right (3).

weather.heading: Dire Weather
weather.text: When travelling in lands at the mercy of dire weather, roll at the start of each Phase.

rows.dire: Dire weather. You can’t leave the Hex and can’t get proper sleep.
rows.looming: Looming threat. If this is rolled a second consecutive time, treat as dire weather.

mood.heading: Local Mood
mood.text: When arriving in a Holding, roll to gauge the local mood.

rows.woe: Occupied by a looming or recent woe.
rows.decline: There is a sense of things in decline.
rows.fine: A fine mood and all seems well enough.

land.heading: The Lay of the Land
land.text: Each Hex is large and diverse, a land within the land. Some may spend their whole lives within one. A forest Hex might have cliffs, streams, clearings, and caves.
land.note: Use Spark Tables (p22) and the prompts at the base of each Knight and Myth spread to help fill the blanks in your Hexes.

actions.heading: Exploration Actions
actions.text: When ruling exploration actions, follow the standard Action Procedure (p16). In particular, consider whether the action will take a whole Phase of the day to carry out.
actions.note: As with other Actions, the players should know the risks before they commit to it.

saves.heading: Saves
saves.text: If the Action calls for a Save the Company decides who rolls, using their Virtue. Even if they fail the Save, the goal might still be achievable, but now faces an obstacle, a hostile encounter, or an additional cost. While the cause and consequence of failure can be personal, they also represent the whims of nature, bad weather, shifting land.
saves.lead: If it is unclear which Virtue to use, consider the main activity involved in the risky part:

searching.heading: Searching
searching.text: It takes a whole Phase to carry out a surface level sweep of an entire Hex, thoroughly search for something known to exist there, or find a vantage point.

vision.heading: Vision
vision.text: From a vantage point it’s possible to get an overview of the current Hex and a general sense of what lies in neighbouring hexes, but not specific details.

folklore.text: Everybody knows something about Myths. How much depends on who they are.

vassals.label: Vassals
vassals.text: know about their nearest Myth, and its general direction. If it is adjacent to their home then they know its precise location. They know Landmarks in their home and neighbouring Hexes.

roamers.label: Knights and Vagabonds
roamers.text: have roamed enough to know about a random Myth of the Realm and its rough direction. They also know of the nearest Landmark.

everyone.label: All of the above
everyone.text: know rumours that warn of dangers, but not how to avoid or undo them.

seers.label: Seers
seers.text: know the rules of all Myths, their secrets, and their locations. They know their weaknesses, and cures to their maladies. They know all Landmarks in the Realm. Such vast knowledge isn’t given freely.

restoreOpenSheets.name: Reopen Sheets on Reload
restoreOpenSheets.hint: Reopen the Knight, item and journal sheets and the rulebook you had open, where you left them, when you reload Foundry. Only affects this browser.

rulebook.title: Mythic Bastionland
rulebook.nobodyToShow: No one else is signed in to show the page to.
rulebook.noCopy: The GM hasn’t given this world a copy of the rulebook yet.
rulebook.otherEdition: This PDF has {pages} pages, but the rulebook this system’s page numbers come from has {expected}, so a jump to a page may land in the wrong place.
rulebook.notPdf: That file doesn’t look like a PDF. It’s been saved anyway, in case it is one.
rulebook.copying: Copying the rulebook into the world…
rulebook.copied: The rulebook is ready to read.
rulebook.copyFailed: The rulebook couldn’t be copied into the world. Check that you’re allowed to upload files and that there’s space.
rulebook.keepFailed: The rulebook was copied in, but the world couldn’t record where it went.

keybinding.name: Open the Rulebook
keybinding.hint: Open the rulebook, or close it when it’s already in front.

forPlayers.name: Let Players Open the Rulebook
forPlayers.hint: Players get the Rulebook button and hotkey too. Pages the GM shows them open either way.

setup.title: Your Rulebook
setup.intro: Point this world at your own copy of the Mythic Bastionland PDF to read it in Foundry’s PDF viewer, with its chapters, search and page links.
setup.choose: Choose a File on This Computer
setup.copyHint: A file chosen from this computer is copied to {dir} in your Foundry data folder, so it’s still there next session. Forgetting it leaves the file there.
setup.whoCanRead: Foundry serves everything in its data folder to anyone signed into the world who knows the path, so treat the copy as shared with your table.
setup.hotkey: Press B to open or close the rulebook. Change the key under Configure Controls.

welcome.title: Welcome to Mythic Bastionland
welcome.hint: The window a new world opens with, where your rulebook PDF is brought in.
welcome.lead: You are Knights, united by a common Oath and visions of the City. You may have dreams of glory, but every Knight must accept the risk of death.

book.heading: Your Rulebook
book.intro: The rulebook doesn’t come with this system. If you own the PDF, the {pages}-page one, choose it here and this world is filled in from it.

art.label: Import the art and tables
art.hint: Every Knight’s, Seer’s and Myth’s picture, the text the choosers fill characters in from, the Spark Tables, and compendiums of Arms & Goods. The PDF is read in your browser, and what’s taken from it is saved to {root} in your Foundry data folder.

keep.label: A copy to read in Foundry
keep.hint: Always kept. Opens with B, or the Rulebook button in the Journal tab, with its chapters and search. It’s copied to {dir} in your Foundry data folder, which anyone signed into the world can fetch if they know the path.
keep.done: This world reads its rulebook from

book.later: Later on, Import PDF on the hotbar and the Rulebook button in the Journal tab each do one of these again.

knights.text: Create Actor in the Actors tab makes a Knight, then offers to roll or pick one from the book.

realms.text: New Realm in the Scenes tab draws a Realm map to explore, hex by hex.

sites.text: New Site in the Journal tab, or on the hotbar, maps a Site that players see as they explore it.

referee.text: Referee Rolls, Spark Tables, Time and the GM Toolkit, where the Myths and their Omens are kept, wait in the Roll Tables tab.
